title: apache/commons-numbers#223: ArithmeticUtils.pow accepts (-2)^31, found and confined from bytecode
summary: A pull request that lets `ArithmeticUtils.pow(int, int)` return `Integer.MIN_VALUE` for `(-2)^31` instead of throwing. The regression proof found the one changed input, `pow(-2, 31)`, from the two versions' bytecode in 185 s; the Javadoc was proved on the new version; and the change was proved confined to that input on all 2^64 others in 18 minutes.
verdictLabel: ✗ the intended change found; ✓ confined to it; ✓ Javadoc proved
notes: Next: `pow(long, int)`, which the same pull request changed and the recorded run did not reach.
The confined-change proof did not finish in the default 300 s and took 1083 s with `--timeout 1500`: budget proofs over two full `int` ranges in tens of minutes.

Migrated to the external-target route on 2026-11-14 by the positive stream of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md (its P5): target.json, sources.lock.json, claims/, replay/, controls/ and records/ were added; README.md, the summary and the verdict label are the historical report of 2026-11-01 and stay as written. A receipt of the new route goes beside them, never in their place.

Revisions resolved afresh from github.com: before e7c172d2 (the only parent of the squash merge), after 8cfc04e8 (the merge), and the pull request's head 79aa4643, whose ArithmeticUtils.java is after's blob. Maven Central's commons-numbers-core 1.3 carries before's file (blob 153b3202, in its sources JAR too) and the same bytecode as that file compiled alone; no release carries after's, so the route is the upstream Maven build of each commit (runtime's preparation, not yet run).

The selected A5 obligation is claims/pow-minus-two.json: for k == -2 and 0 <= e <= 31, pow(int,int) returns (-2)^e. Native strict, expected established on after and refuted on before at (-2, 31), the witness the replay reproduces. It reaches no gap: jvmcontract gaps lists only the StringBuilder calls of the e < 0 message (records/pow-gaps.json), which its assume excludes. The report's confined-change row is predicted refused under strict for exactly those gaps.

Hand replay on 2026-11-14 (a note, not evidence): ArithmeticUtils.java of each commit compiled alone with JDK 11's javac --release 8, plus Central's 1.3 JAR, each with the driver (driver.jar sha256 315ecf00…) in its own JVM on JDK 21 and 25, over the 75 probes. controls/oracle.py: after meets the Javadoc's contract on all 75; before and 1.3 give byte-identical output and deviate at (-2, 31) alone (ArithmeticException); the property holds on all 32 points at after and fails at e = 31 alone at before. Checked with the wrong revision's output and a truncated file, the oracle fails, as it should.

Runner interface (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5 step 1, request 9): controls/oracle.py also defines driver_args(), the driver's whole argument vector (the same as `oracle.py argv`), and problems(lines), one revision's driver lines in, [(probe, problem)] out, where the independent statement disagrees; an exception is a replay that can't be judged, never a violation. runtime.run_controls passes driver_args() and keeps every line the driver prints, its preparation copies the probes file with the oracle, and workflow_ingest reads each revision with problems() against what its pair's kind expects (examples/tools/targets/runtime.py's docstring). Before this, the merged runner looked for a PROBES list and ingestion called check(lines), so the controls could not have run; problems() reads the Javadoc's contract (rules 1-3) without the declared deviations, which are what the exact fix's pair expects of before (it violates, at (-2)^31) and after (it holds); the probes file's constant is now PROBES_FILE, so the runner never takes the path for a PROBES list. The CLI (`argv`, `check`, the pair comparison) is unchanged.
